clue.text: Celebrity's sweetheart left shed

indicators.note: to shed something is to cast it off, so the named letter drops out of the word

parts.note: an old flame is a former sweetheart
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A star's lover has walked out and been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L out of FLAME to leave FAME; the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity as a state of being widely known is a straightforward synonym for renown.

clue.text: Steps outside?

parts.note: surface reading: someone walks out of a door; setter's reading: a staircase fixed to the exterior of a building, used in an emergency

explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' reads as a verb, but it is a noun: a flight of stairs on the outside of a building for escaping a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency staircase bolted to the exterior wall is literally a set of steps outside.

clue.text: Agencies for spiritualists?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: means or channels through which something is conveyed, with the regular plural
second meaning: practitioners who claim to pass messages from the dead

explanation.surface: Are there agencies that cater for people who believe in spirits?
explanation.walkthrough: The plural ending matters: 'media' is usual for channels of communication, but the psychic sense always takes the regular plural, which the second meaning confirms.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both an intermediate means of transmission and a psychic who acts as a go-between with the dead.

clue.text: Tearful, complete killjoy

parts.note: wet as in damp-eyed
blanket as an adjective means total or covering everything

explanation.surface: Someone is crying and ruining everyone's fun.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a person who dampens enthusiasm, just as a soaked cover smothers a fire.

clue.text: Insincere, some unkempt yobbos

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Scruffy louts make hollow promises.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty words or gestures are hollow ones, lacking real feeling, hence insincere.

clue.text: Cheers weaver and son, winning

parts.note: Nick Bottom is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
S is the abbreviation for son
a team that is up is ahead

explanation.surface: A toast to a weaver and his son, who are winning.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are drinking toasts said before downing a glass.

clue.text: Tape-record him, invalid leaving war memorial

indicators.note: invalid read as not valid, so the letters before it are wrong as they stand and must be rearranged

parts.note: all thirteen letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: An instruction to tape a sick man as he leaves a war memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' looks like a sick person, but read as in-VAL-id it is the anagram signal; 'leaving' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris arch honours those who fought for France, notably in the Revolutionary and Napoleonic wars.

clue.text: Taken out on express, reportedly, in Irish county

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken or heard, so the sound of the words counts, not their spelling

parts.note: taken out means killed, and to express a view is to air it; 'on' places one after the other

explanation.surface: Someone was removed from an express train in an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' suggests a train, but here it is a verb meaning to voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Kildare is a county in the province of Leinster, west of Dublin.

clue.text: Head brought over a large fish

indicators.note: brought over suggests something turned upside down, which in a down entry reverses the word's order

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
taken as written

explanation.surface: A large fish's head was brought across.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuna is a big ocean fish of the mackerel family, some weighing hundreds of kilos.

clue.text: On which a VIP may walk in resort with dog, for example

definitions.text: On which a VIP may walk

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside resort town in North Yorkshire
a dog is one example of a pet

explanation.surface: A celebrity strolls through a seaside town with a pet dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' tempts as an anagram signal, but it names a particular English seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Dignitaries arriving at premieres or state visits walk along a crimson strip of floor covering.

clue.text: A welcome suggestion involving police officer — end argument amicably?

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the suggestion word wraps around the officer's title

parts.note: taken as written
to greet is to welcome
an offer is a proposal or suggestion
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A friendly proposal involving a policeman settles a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both sides accept that they disagree and drop the quarrel without rancour.

clue.text: Settlement mostly in Costa Rican currency

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a colony is a settlement founded abroad

explanation.surface: Talk of a settlement largely using Costa Rica's money.
explanation.definitionFit: The colón, named after Columbus, is the monetary unit of Costa Rica.

clue.text: European with question about king — he may be able to answer it

definitions.text: he may be able to answer it

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: about means around, so the question word goes round the royal letter

parts.note: a query is a question
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A European asks a question about the king, which a courtier might answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' refers back to the question about the king: a royal aide is the one to answer it.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is an officer attending a member of the royal family, so well placed to field questions about the monarch.

clue.text: In time to come a doyen must change

indicators.note: must change says the letters cannot stay in their current order

parts.note: fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Eventually even a senior figure will have to adapt.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase points to an unspecified moment in the future, as in 'some day'.

clue.text: Generally, any garbled composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are assembled afresh

parts.note: fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Broadly speaking, any piece of music played badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garbled' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'composition' does the signalling.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means on the whole or for the most part, matching 'generally' as an adverb.

clue.text: An uplifting act in a theatre?

definitions.text: An uplifting act in a theatre?

parts.words: An uplifting act in a theatre?
parts.note: surface reading: a cheering performance on stage; setter's reading: a procedure such as a facelift, done in an operating theatre

explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' means inspiring on the surface but literally a lift of the face; 'theatre' is the hospital operating room.
explanation.definitionFit: Facelifts and similar beauty operations are carried out by surgeons in operating theatres.

clue.text: In New York must wear a suit no matter what

indicators.note: something worn goes around the wearer, so the clothing word surrounds the place

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a lawsuit is a case in court
NY is the abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: In Manhattan you have to wear a suit, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' suggests clothing, but it is a legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means regardless of circumstances, the same as whatever happens.

clue.text: We, say, in New Orleans on run with pop

indicators.note: new means made fresh, so the letters that follow are reformed in a fresh order

parts.note: fodder
fodder
fodder
fodder

explanation.surface: We, perhaps, in New Orleans, out on the town drinking soda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Orleans' reads as the city, but 'New' is the signal and only 'Orleans' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: 'We' is a grammatical example of a word standing for the speaker group, a first-person plural of that category.

clue.text: Managed to continue in Burma's capital

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
to go on is to continue

explanation.surface: Someone managed to keep going in the Burmese capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon, now Yangon, was the capital of Burma (Myanmar) until 2006.

clue.text: Baltimore baseball team ring positions I occupied

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: occupied means filled by someone, so the letter sits inside the word for positions

parts.note: roles are positions or parts
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fielding positions in a ballpark taken by one player.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltimore Orioles are the city's Major League team, named after the state bird of Maryland.

clue.text: Scruffy, a French cartoonist

parts.note: un is French for a
Bill Tidy was a British cartoonist famous for his Punch and Private Eye work

explanation.surface: A shabby French cartoonist.
explanation.walkthrough: The cartoonist's name means neat, yet with the French article in front the whole means the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy and scruffy both describe a messy, unkempt appearance.

clue.text: Pages unwell after drill — stimulant required

indicators.note: after says the words before it come second, so the drill piece leads and the pages and illness follow it

parts.note: PE, physical education, was once known as drill in schools
pp is the abbreviation for pages
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: After exercise, pages feel sick and need a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the drill piece first, ahead of the pages and illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A pep pill is an amphetamine-type tablet taken to boost energy, so a stimulant.

clue.text: Ancient city, favourite with artist

parts.note: a teacher's pet is a favourite
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: An old city is popular with painters.
explanation.definitionFit: Petra is the rock-cut Nabataean city in Jordan, over two thousand years old.

clue.text: Body ring

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a group of people acting together

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests body piercing jewellery, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an organised group of people and a hoop of metal worn on a finger.

clue.text: Detached, a goose flying back

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: flying back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a goose is a silly person

explanation.surface: A wild goose, set apart, heads home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goose' looks like the bird but means a simpleton.
explanation.definitionFit: An aloof person keeps a cool distance from others, emotionally detached.

clue.text: A red alert worried one who has a gallery, maybe

definitions.text: one who has a gallery, maybe

indicators.note: worried means agitated or disturbed, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A security alarm alarmed the gallery owner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone selling paintings commonly runs premises where works are shown, though 'maybe' admits not all do.

clue.text: Fast food dish finished by baker abroad, first in bistro

parts.note: done means finished

indicators.note: abroad means away from home and scattered about, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

parts.note: fodder for the rearrangement

indicators.note: first in asks for the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A takeaway snack is finished off by a baker working overseas, first served in a bistro.
explanation.definitionFit: Slices of spit-roasted meat in pitta are a classic takeaway eaten late at night.

clue.text: Dogs, perhaps, restricted by this leash

indicators.note: restricted by means held within, so the answer is penned inside the next words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Dogs are kept in check by this lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogs' looks like animals on a leash, but it is the Isle of Dogs, a district of East London in a bend of the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Dogs is a named island-like area, so it is one example of the island word.
